subject.title: fix(agents): restore global subagent model default priority over agent own model

question: Should isolated cron use the documented global-subagent-default-first precedence already used by native subagent spawn planning, even when the named target agent has its own model?
rationale: Both orderings originated in merged bug fixes for legitimate but competing expectations, and changing the shared helper alters existing model/provider routing rather than repairing an undisputed implementation typo.

options.title: Unify on global default
options.body: Use per-agent subagent model first, global subagent default second, and agent model last across native spawn and isolated cron paths.

options.title: Preserve cron agent specificity
options.body: Keep isolated cron agent-first and explicitly document and test that it intentionally differs from native subagent spawning.

recommendation.title: Unify on global default
recommendation.body: Use per-agent subagent model first, global subagent default second, and agent model last across native spawn and isolated cron paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent merged ownership of the shared isolated-cron selector and fallback policy is in this person’s work.
